summary: This informational document defines and registers the value "impp" (instant messaging and presence protocol) for the "purpose" parameter of the SIP Call-Info header field.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds the impp label to SIP Call-Info. The label identifies a URI for an instant messaging and presence protocol, and the document notes related security and privacy concerns.

questions: what does impp mean in a sip call-info header
can impp identify protocols other than xmpp
what privacy issue does rfc 6993 identify
subtitle: Registers impp as a purpose value for SIP Call-Info links to messaging addresses.

tldr.problem: Some endpoints support both SIP and instant messaging, and SIP needed a way to identify a Call-Info link used for messaging and presence.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers impp as a predefined value for the purpose parameter of the SIP Call-Info header.
tldr.outcome: The value can identify an instant messaging and presence URI, including but not limited to XMPP; the RFC warns about spoofing and privacy.

today: RFC 6993 is an Informational RFC. The unit metadata does not list it as obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: The impp Purpose Value
sections.content:
Some real-time communication endpoints support both the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) and the Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol (XMPP). The RFC says it can help interoperability to advertise a SIP address over XMPP and an XMPP address over SIP.

RFC 6993 registers impp, meaning instant messaging and presence protocol, as the value of the purpose parameter in the SIP Call-Info header. A URI for a protocol other than XMPP may also be used.
sections.plainLanguage: The impp value identifies a Call-Info link used for instant messaging and presence. The linked URI may refer to XMPP or another such protocol.

sections.title: Using Call-Info
sections.content:
The RFC gives an example in which a Call-Info header contains an XMPP URI and the parameter purpose=impp. This associates the link with instant messaging and presence rather than leaving its purpose unspecified.

The value is registered in the SIP Parameters registry as a predefined value for the Call-Info purpose parameter.
sections.plainLanguage: A Call-Info header can carry an instant messaging URI with the purpose value impp. The registry makes that value recognizable.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
Advertising an XMPP address over SIP could reveal another way to contact or attack an endpoint. The purpose parameter could be spoofed, so a receiving endpoint ought to check it against an authoritative source. Clients can protect the header's integrity and confidentiality using S/MIME end to end or TLS hop by hop.

Linking SIP and messaging identifiers may be privacy-sensitive. User agents ought to let users control whether these values are sent.
sections.plainLanguage: A false link could mislead a recipient, and linking two addresses may reveal private information. The RFC recommends verification, protection and user control.
